trust_decision.summary: Whether a client-supplied request-header value may be written to the DEBUG log is decided by name lookup in a four-entry denylist inside LoggingMiddleware._sanitize_headers, applied only to the client headers dict; any header name not on that list is logged verbatim.

landing_point.why: The only code that writes client-supplied request data to a log file is the DEBUG 'Client headers' line, and the helper it calls (logging.py:35-48) holds the credential name list; the advisory summary (sensitive information into a log file) leads straight here.

fix_sites.entry_point: foreman-mcp-server CLI (pyproject.toml:24-25) in default streamable-http transport -> MCP HTTP endpoint -> LoggingMiddleware.on_message (server.py:179), which calls _log_client_info -> _sanitize_headers

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The other data reaching the same log line is MCP session metadata (client_id, client_params), which a solver would call protocol metadata rather than the credentials the advisory names, so the header-only fix is treated as complete.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Non-secret values must stay readable in the debug log: foreman_username and mcp-session-id are deliberately allowlisted by the published fix (the review commit adds foreman_username to the list and its test asserts the value 'admin' passes through), so a mask-everything fix or a stop-logging-headers fix breaks the legitimate debugging output the server is built to emit at --log-level debug.

O6_input_shapes: header names that are not on any credential list (e.g. x-custom-secret, x-api-key) - masked by default under the allowlist
case-varied header keys (Host, CONTENT-TYPE, Foreman_Token) - compared via key.lower()
allowlisted non-secret headers (host, user-agent, content-type, foreman_username, mcp-session-id) - passed through unchanged

O8_uncovered_routes.route: MCP session client parameters are logged verbatim at DEBUG with no redaction, while only the headers mapping passes through _sanitize_headers
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: client_params are MCP initialize metadata (protocol version, capabilities, clientInfo name/version), not credential fields, and the advisory is about HTTP request headers
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file and same function as the fix site

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an effective-configuration log line at startup (e.g. logger.info(ctx.params)) that dumps the --foreman-password / FOREMAN_PASSWORD value
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the CLI callback already receives foreman_password in scope (server.py:132) next to an existing logger.error call (server.py:150), and logging the effective configuration at startup is a routine maintainer habit; the header allowlist does not transfer to a config dict, so this needs its own mechanism

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a _sanitize_params / _sanitize_client_params companion applied to the client_params debug line, mirroring _sanitize_headers
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the same function already prints three other client-controlled fields raw, so a maintainer fixing this log line would plausibly add a second sanitizer call rather than remove the line

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a debug log of the outgoing Foreman request headers built by mcp_info_headers, which would print the mcp-session-id value
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: header forwarding to Foreman is exactly the kind of glue code people log while debugging proxy/session problems, and it reuses header values that the logging allowlist treats as safe

O9_family: insertion of sensitive information into a log file (CWE-532), credential disclosure through DEBUG logging

O10_build.toolchain: uv + hatchling (pyproject.toml:27-29), pytest and ruff as dev group (pyproject.toml:18-22); runtime deps fastmcp>=2.13.0,<2.14.0, apypie, aiofiles, rpds-py (pyproject.toml:11-16); uv.lock present
O10_build.project_tests: pytest suite under tests/ (middleware, tools, resources), run by CI as `uv run pytest` (.github/workflows/ci.yml:62-68); the affected area has no tests at the pinned commit - tests/middleware/ holds only __init__.py and test_auth.py, and the fix adds tests/middleware/test_logging.py as a new file

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: extend the existing four-name denylist with authorization / x-api-key / cookie instead of switching to an allowlist

out_of_scope_notes: FastMCP's own ErrorHandlingMiddleware (server.py:177) and the ASGI server access log may also emit request data; they live outside this repository and were not examined.
unverified: Repo size in MB was not measured (no shell available in this session); the tree has 31 Python source files with no vendored binaries or assets, so tiny_repo (under 5 MB source) is an inference from file inventory, not a measurement.

Whether fastmcp's session.client_params can ever carry credentials depends on the MCP/InitializeRequestParams schema outside this repository; the O8 route is listed on the pinned code that logs it verbatim, and present_in_latest is unknown because no latest release was supplied for O8.
